newsitem.title: INDIA: India to allow millers to import wheat.
newsitem.headline: India to allow millers to import wheat.

text.p: India's Commerce Ministry said on Friday it would allow millers to import wheat under licence, in a bid to stem rising domestic prices of the cereal.

"Roller flour mills have been permitted to freely import wheat to meet their own requirements for milling purposes and for sale of the resultant flour in the domestic market," a ministry statement said.

But it warned that the millers would first have to register their import contracts with the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA), which will monitor the actual imports made against the contracts.
It said such imports would be strictly subject to actual user conditions and would have to be completed before March 31, 1997.
The Indian government late on Thursday said it would import two million tonnes of wheat in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) to augment domestic supplies and check rising prices.
Dealers said wheat prices had softened by about 1,000 rupees per tonne on news of the move, and they expected them to fall sharply after arrivals began in January.
